- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25), model often overpredicts; reduce forecast to reflect bearish pressure.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days); apply a 1-2 day lag correction to smooth out overreaction.  
- In periods of strong mean reversion (e.g., 30d price dropping from 80+ to 60+), model tends to overcorrect; adjust forecast downward by 2-5% of recent range.  
- For 30d forecasts, if last 3-5 days show strong upward trend, model often fails to capture continuation; add 1-3% buffer to forecast if sentiment remains positive.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model is prone to flat or slightly downward bias; add 0.5-1.5% upward adjustment to avoid underestimating volatility.
